title: Cubby Fundamentals
description: Cubby, the software Greens runs its storage sites on: where things live, finding an open unit, leads, reservations and move-ins, how a tenant ledger works with worked examples, taking payments and cards by phone, waives, credits and refunds, transfers and move-outs, overlocks, liens and exemptions, gate codes, notes and tasks, and the open and close routine with its reports.
overview: What Cubby is, the words it uses, and first-of-month billing with jump day 26
Finding your way around and finding an open unit by size
Leads, reservations and the move-in, in order
How a ledger works, the paid-through date and days past due, with worked examples
Taking payments safely, AutoPay and the failed AutoPay call
Waives, credits, refunds, transfers and move-outs
Overlocks, liens and exemptions as Cubby shows them
Gate codes, notes, tasks, the open and close, and a one-page job aid

questions.q: A tenant who moved in on 11/18 asks why her first payment was so much smaller than her rent. What do you tell her?
options: She got a first-month discount for new tenants
Rent is due on the 1st, so it was shortened
The first payment was a deposit and rent comes later
Her rent will be due on the 18th of every month
questions.explanation: Greens bills on the 1st. A mid-month move-in pays only the days left in the month. It is proration, not a discount, and there is no deposit on new move-ins.

questions.q: A customer rents a $120.00 unit with no protection plan on 11/27. What does he pay at move-in, with the $25.00 Administration Fee?
questions.explanation: 11/27 is on or after jump day 26: 4 days of November (120 x 4 / 30 = $16.00) plus all of December ($120.00) plus $25.00 = $161.00. $41.00 forgets December.

questions.q: You see a unit with nobody renting it on the sitemap. It is always available to rent.
questions.explanation: False. Vacant means not leased AND rentable. An empty unit can be marked unrentable, for repairs or cleaning, and cannot be rented until that is cleared.

questions.q: A caller needs a covered space for a 28 ft trailer. What is the fastest way to find one in Cubby?
options: Walk the lot and look for empty covered spaces
Filter pricing groups by size and covered
Open last month's Rent Roll and look for vacancies
Ask the caller to search the website instead
questions.explanation: Filter the pricing groups by size and features with Pricing group is Available on. A walk or an old report misses what was rented this morning.

questions.q: Your site has nothing open in the size a walk-in needs. What do you do in Cubby?
options: Offer an unrentable unit at a lower rate
Check nearby Greens sites for that size
Tell her to call back next month
Rent her a smaller unit without asking
questions.explanation: View nearby facilities shows the same size at other Greens sites. If nothing fits, save a lead. Never offer an unrentable unit.

questions.q: A caller says he found Greens by searching online and will visit Saturday. What do you save before you hang up?
options: A lead with source Other and no follow-up task
A lead, source Search engine, and a task
A reservation with a reservation fee
Nothing until he actually comes in
questions.explanation: Every caller who does not rent today is a lead with the real source, and every promised follow-up is a task. Greens charges no reservation fee.

questions.q: During a move-in the card payment shows pending. What do you do?
options: Run the card again right away to be safe
Hand over the code and finish up
Wait, check again, ask your manager
Take the same amount in cash too
questions.explanation: A pending payment has an unknown outcome. Running it again can charge twice; no gate code or lock until it shows succeeded.

questions.q: On a move-in, Cubby prorates the protection plan the same way it prorates rent.
questions.explanation: True. Greens' ledgers show protection prorated by days used over days in the month, just like rent, so a mid-month move-in pays a partial protection line.

questions.q: A walk-in is finishing her move-in for an RV space. Which must be done before she leaves?
options: Her photo ID checked and approved
The vehicle plate, state and type entered
questions.explanation: Nothing leaves the counter Incomplete: signed lease, ID, vehicle details and proof of insurance. New move-ins pay no deposit and Greens charges no reservation fee.

questions.q: Rent is $120.00. A tenant moves in on 11/21 (November has 30 days). What is the prorated rent?
questions.explanation: 11/21 through 11/30 is 10 days, counting both. 120.00 x 10 / 30 = $40.00. $36.00 counts only 9 days.

questions.q: Rent is $120.00, no plan, move-in 11/28. What is due at move-in, with the $25.00 Administration Fee?
questions.explanation: On or after jump day 26: 3 days of November ($12.00) plus December ($120.00) plus $25.00 = $157.00. $37.00 forgets December.

questions.q: A tenant takes a $14.00 protection plan and moves in on 11/18. What is the prorated protection line?
questions.explanation: 11/18 through 11/30 is 13 days. 14.00 x 13 / 30 = 6.066..., rounded to $6.07. Protection is prorated like rent.

questions.q: December rent of $150.00 and protection of $14.00 posted on 12/01. On 12/04 the tenant pays $100.00. How much rent is still open?
questions.explanation: Charges posted together are paid rent first. $100.00 goes to rent, leaving $50.00 of rent plus all $14.00 of protection open.

questions.q: A lease is paid through 10/31. Today is 11/16. How many days past due is it?
questions.explanation: Days past due = today minus the paid-through date, minus 1. 11/16 minus 10/31 is 16; minus 1 = 15.

questions.q: Today is 12/10. A November rent posted on 11/01 is still open. Where does Aged Receivables put it?
questions.explanation: 11/01 to 12/01 is 30 days, plus 9 to 12/10 = 39 days: the 30-60 bucket.

questions.q: Rent $95.00 plus a $14.00 plan. Paid through 11/30, the tenant pays $327.00 on 11/20. What prepaid is left after the 01/01 charges post?
questions.explanation: All $327.00 becomes prepaid. Each month uses $109.00: $218.00 after 12/01, $109.00 after 01/01. Paid-through is then 01/31.

questions.q: A balance of $172.50 includes a $22.50 CA Late Fee. You waive the fee. What is the balance now?
questions.explanation: A waive cancels that one charge now: 172.50 - 22.50 = $150.00. A credit would have left today's balance unchanged.

questions.q: Rent is $160.00 and the tenant has a 5% discount program. What is the net due for the month?
questions.explanation: The rent posts at $160.00 and the discount posts as its own line of $8.00. Net: $152.00.

questions.q: A tenant's $129.00 rent payment is refunded, and the rent charge is not waived. What does the tenant owe afterward?
questions.explanation: A refund reopens the charge it paid. Without a waive of the rent, the $129.00 is owed again.

questions.q: Cubby lists a unit as needing an overlock, but the lease shows a Payment Arrangement exemption. What do you do?
options: Overlock it, since Cubby listed it
Skip it and tell your manager
Overlock it and remove it tomorrow
questions.explanation: Never overlock a unit with an exemption. Skip it and tell your manager that Cubby still flagged it.

questions.q: A delinquency exemption also stops rent from posting on the 1st.
questions.explanation: False. An exemption pauses chosen collection steps (late fees, overlock, lien eligibility, collection messages). Rent still posts.

questions.q: Before starting a lien, you see a note that the tenant mentioned being deployed. What now?
options: Start the lien; deployment is private
Stop and tell your manager today
Start it and add a note about it
Send the notice by text instead
questions.explanation: A tenant on active duty, or within 90 days after it, may not have a lien enforced without a court order. Stop and escalate.

questions.q: A tenant in the lien process pays all the rent but none of the lien fees. Where does that leave the lien?
options: It stops, because rent is paid
It goes on until fees are paid too
It ends after a manager waives rent
questions.explanation: Only payment in full, including posted fees, stops the lien. Tell your manager the same day when a lien tenant pays in full.

questions.q: You called a tenant for the 6th's past-due task and got voicemail. What do you do with the task?
options: Leave it open for tomorrow's shift
Delete it and make a new one
questions.explanation: A call with no answer is a call made. Complete it with a note: no answer, voicemail left, payment link sent. Archived means not done.

questions.q: It is fine to leave a tenant's new gate code in a voicemail if they asked for a call back.
questions.explanation: False. Give a code in person or on the phone after confirming who you are speaking with, never in a voicemail or a text.

questions.q: A tenant says, "Someone changed my gate code, I never asked." Where do you look first?
options: The notes on the pricing group
questions.explanation: Every change on a lease is in its Activity record, with who did it and when, or that Cubby did it by itself.

questions.q: A coworker offers to sign you in with her account so you can waive a fee your role cannot. What do you do?
options: Accept, since it is only one fee
Use her sign-in and note it
Waive it from the phone app
questions.explanation: Every action carries the name of whoever is signed in. A missing button is usually your role; ask your manager.

questions.q: A tenant at a Greens site who moves in on the 26th pays for the rest of this month plus all of next month at move-in.
questions.explanation: True. Jump day is 26, so a move-in on or after the 26th also pays the next full month, and the first regular bill is the 1st of the month after next.

questions.q: It is the start of your shift. Where do you see today's tasks, move-ins, move-outs and new online rentals together?
questions.explanation: The Home tab is where every shift starts: what needs someone today.

questions.q: A tenant with two leases calls to pay. What do you confirm before you take the money?
options: Only the last four of the card
questions.explanation: One contact can hold several leases, at more than one site. Confirm the person and the lease before you change anything.

questions.q: A pricing group in your search says No availability. What does that tell you?
options: Nothing of that type is open now
The rate has not been set yet
The units are all reserved for staff
Cubby is still loading the units
questions.explanation: No availability means every unit in that pricing group is leased or unrentable right now.

questions.q: When you search for a unit, you pick the pricing group first and then the exact unit.
questions.explanation: True. Cubby sells by pricing group (size and kind with one rate); you choose the group, then the unit, and check it on the sitemap.

questions.q: A caller is a current tenant asking about a second unit. Cubby shows Active lead found. What do you choose?
questions.explanation: Continue the existing lead rather than making a duplicate contact or lead.

questions.q: A customer with a reservation for 12/01 calls to cancel. What do you do?
options: Leave it open in case he changes his mind
Cancel it and note the reason
Convert it so the unit stays held
questions.explanation: Cancel it so the unit goes back on the market, with a note. Greens charges no reservation fee.

questions.q: Which lead status does Cubby set by itself, not you?
questions.explanation: You set New, In progress, On hold and Unqualified. Cubby sets Reservation and Converted when those happen.

questions.q: A customer storing a boat is on the Configure move-in screen. What must you tick?
options: Custom rate for the vehicle space
questions.explanation: Tick Tenant is storing a vehicle for every vehicle, boat or trailer. Leave the waive boxes alone unless your manager approved it.

questions.q: The card for a move-in is declined. The customer asks for her gate code anyway. What do you say?
options: I'll text it once you get home
You can use the master code today
questions.explanation: No gate code or lock until the payment succeeds. Ask for another card or method.

questions.q: A tenant has her own insurance. What do you enter on the coverage step?
options: The Greens plan at the lowest level
No coverage, since she is insured
Nothing until she brings a copy
questions.explanation: For the tenant's own policy, enter the policy number and a future expiration date, and collect proof of insurance.

questions.q: A tenant says, "I paid by card on the 3rd," but the ledger shows no payment that day. What is the most likely reason?
options: It was applied to next month
It was turned into a credit
questions.explanation: A declined card posts nothing to the ledger. Check with the tenant and offer another method or a payment link.

questions.q: A tenant was charged a late fee that should not have posted. Which tool takes it off today's balance?
questions.explanation: A waive cancels that one charge now. A credit waits for the next bill, and a refund sends money back.

questions.q: A tenant's bank payment from last week comes back returned. What happens to the ledger?
options: Cubby waives the rent for the month
questions.explanation: A returned bank payment is marked failed, which reopens the charges it had paid. Call the tenant; the balance is owed again.

questions.q: Giving a tenant a credit lowers the balance they owe today.
questions.explanation: False. A credit waits on the lease and is used on the next recurring charges. A waive is what lowers today's balance.

questions.q: A lease is paid through 09/30. Today is 11/04. How many days past due is it?
questions.explanation: 11/04 minus 09/30 is 35 days; minus 1 = 34.

questions.q: A tenant owes $129.00 rent and $14.00 protection, both posted on the 1st, and pays $129.00 on the 5th. What is still open?
questions.explanation: Posted together, rent is paid before protection. The $129.00 pays the rent; the protection stays open, so the month is not fully paid.

questions.q: It is the 11th and a tenant still owes part of this month's rent. What does Cubby post overnight?
questions.explanation: CA Late Fee posts by itself on the 11th. CA Preliminary Lien Notice follows on the 15th.

questions.q: A tenant who pays three months ahead is shown paid through the end of the third month right away.
questions.explanation: False. Prepaid money moves the paid-through date one month at a time, as each month's charges post and are paid from it.

questions.q: Rent is $150.00 with a $14.00 plan. Move-in is 11/18. What is due, with the $25.00 Administration Fee?
questions.explanation: 13 days: rent $65.00 plus protection $6.07 (14 x 13 / 30) plus $25.00 = $96.07. $90.00 leaves out the protection.

questions.q: Rent is $90.00, no plan, move-in 11/26. What is the rent part of the move-in total?
questions.explanation: 11/26 is on jump day: 5 days of November (90 x 5 / 30 = $15.00) plus December ($90.00) = $105.00 of rent.

questions.q: In February a tenant asks why her bill doubled. She moved in with a two-month 50% off promotion. What do you show her?
options: A rate increase on her unit this month
questions.explanation: The rent never changed on the ledger; the discount was its own line for two months, then ended.

questions.q: Rent is $180.00, paid through 11/30. On 11/15 the tenant pays $540.00. What does the ledger show on 11/16?
questions.explanation: Nothing is open on 11/15, so all of it becomes prepaid and the paid-through date stays 11/30 until December's rent posts.

questions.q: A tenant owes October rent $130.00, a $20.00 late fee, a $25.00 notice fee and November rent $130.00. She pays $175.00. What is still open?
questions.explanation: Payments go to the oldest charges first: October rent, then the late fee, then the notice fee. November rent stays open.

questions.q: Rent $120.00 and a $14.00 plan post on 12/01. The tenant pays $100.00 on 12/03. What do you tell her is still open?
questions.explanation: Rent is paid first: $20.00 of rent and $14.00 of protection are open, $34.00 in all, and the late fee posts on the 11th if unpaid.

questions.q: A tenant wants to read you her card number over the phone while you are busy with a walk-in. What do you do?
options: Write it down and enter it later
Call back or send a payment link
Ask her to email it to the site
Have her repeat it to the walk-in
questions.explanation: A card goes straight into Cubby, never written down or sent by email. If you cannot enter it now, call back or send a link.

questions.q: A tenant emails his full card number and asks you to run it. What do you do?
options: Run it, then file the email in the lease
Delete it; take the card by phone
Copy it into a lease note
questions.explanation: Never accept a card by email. Delete it, tell him it was deleted, and take the card by phone or send a payment link.

questions.q: Two leases belong to one tenant who wants to pay both from his phone. What do you send?
options: Two separate invoices sent by mail
questions.explanation: One payment link can cover several leases for the same tenant. Check the contact details first.

questions.q: A tenant who pays most of her balance stops the late fee from posting on the 11th.
questions.explanation: False. Only payment in full stops the steps. Tell her what is still open and what posts on the 11th.

questions.q: A first-time late tenant asks you to remove the late fee. It is inside your limit. What reason do you write?
options: Customer asked to have it removed
questions.explanation: Every waive needs a real reason someone can read later. "Customer asked" is not a reason.

questions.q: A tenant was charged twice for the same month by card. Which tool fixes it?
options: Give a credit for next month
questions.explanation: A double payment is refunded. Nothing was charged in error, so there is nothing to waive.

questions.q: A late fee is above your waive limit and the tenant asks for it off. What do you say?
options: Let me check and call you back
Pay half and I'll waive the rest
questions.explanation: Never promise a waive you may not give. Ask your manager and call back the same day.

questions.q: A tenant wants to move from an open space to a covered one at the same site. How do you do it?
options: Move out, then a new rental
A second lease kept with the first
Change the unit on the old lease
questions.explanation: A unit transfer ends the old lease, starts a new one and moves the balance across. A move-out plus a new rental breaks the history and leaves the balance behind.

questions.q: After a unit transfer, what do you check on the old unit?
options: Empty, clean, no tenant lock left
That AutoPay is still turned on for it
That its gate code is enabled
questions.explanation: Walk it: clean and empty stays rentable; a lock left on or a dirty unit gets fixed or marked unrentable.

questions.q: A tenant tells you she is leaving on 01/31. What do you do in Cubby today?
options: Make a Move TNT Out task only
Turn off AutoPay and nothing else
questions.explanation: Schedule it on the lease with the date, notice date, reason and time window, so AutoPay and the reports are right. A task alone is only a reminder.

questions.q: On the move-out day the unit is still full and the tenant has not come in. What do you do?
options: Call, note it, don't complete it
Cut the lock and empty the unit for rent
Turn the gate code back on
questions.explanation: A full unit means the tenant's things are still there and rent continues. Call, note it, and ask your manager before anything else.

questions.q: After a move-out, a small leftover balance can simply be left on the closed lease.
questions.explanation: False. A balance is paid, waived with a reason, refunded or written off by a manager. Each leaves a clear line on the ledger.

questions.q: A tenant whose unit is overlocked pays in full at 2:00 PM. When does the overlock come off?
questions.explanation: Remove it the same day, record it removed, and make sure the gate code works. A paying tenant does not wait.

questions.q: Cubby changes a late tenant's gate code by itself; you do not need to do anything to lock them out at the gate.
questions.explanation: True. Cubby changes the code and sends a gate access notice. Your job is making sure they get a working code once they pay in full.

questions.q: A lease is on the list ready for a lien, but its lease agreement was never signed. What do you do?
options: Start the lien; the list is final
Ask the tenant to sign by text
Start it and fix the paperwork later
questions.explanation: An unsigned lease weakens Greens' position. Tell your manager before a lien starts.

questions.q: A stored trailer's owner is 61 days late. Which path does it follow?
questions.explanation: Vehicles, boats and trailers are never sold through the normal unit auction; the 61st task starts the vehicle path, which your manager runs.

questions.q: Your manager agrees a payment plan with two payments ending 11/30. What end date do you give the exemption?
options: 11/15, the date of the first payment
questions.explanation: Every exemption needs an end date; for a payment arrangement, the day after the last agreed payment. Set a task for the day before it.

questions.q: A tenant's daughter tells you he has died. Which step is yours?
options: Tell your manager the same day
Start the lien to protect Greens
Close the lease and the account
questions.explanation: Exemptions are a manager decision. Note the call and tell your manager, who decides what to pause.

questions.q: A Fairfield tenant's attempts show Unknown user in the access log. What is the likely cause?
questions.explanation: Unknown user means the code is not a current tenant code: an old or mistyped code, or one Cubby changed because the account is late.

questions.q: A tenant completes her move-out. What happens to her gate code?
options: It stays on for a month
It moves to the next tenant
You give it to her family
questions.explanation: Turn the code off at move-out, or check it already is.

questions.q: A tenant's son, not authorized for access, calls asking for the gate code. Where does the answer come from?
options: The pinned note on his contact
questions.explanation: The pinned note shows what every staff member must know before acting, such as who may access the unit.

questions.q: Which of these belongs in a Cubby note?
options: The tenant's full card number for AutoPay
questions.explanation: A good note says what happened, what was agreed and by when. Card numbers, gate codes and opinions never go in a note.

questions.q: A "6th - Call Past Due Tenants" task is open, but the tenant paid through the portal last night. What do you do?
options: Call him to confirm the payment went through
questions.explanation: Check the lease before every call. He paid, so complete the task with a note saying so.

questions.q: Archiving a task records that the work was done.
questions.explanation: False. Archived means dismissed, not done. Use Complete, with a note, for work you did.

questions.q: At close, the drawer is $20.00 short of Cubby's cash payments. What do you do?
options: Leave it for the morning shift to sort out
questions.explanation: Never change a payment to make the drawer match. Recount, look for a payment on the wrong lease or a check entered as cash, and tell your manager.

questions.q: Your manager wants to see which tenants have charges more than 30 days old. Which report?
questions.explanation: Aged Receivables sorts each open charge by age into buckets: 0-30, 30-60 and older.

questions.q: The Rent roll is the list to walk the site against.
questions.explanation: True. Every leased unit should have a tenant and rent; every vacant unit should be rentable or carry a reason.

questions.q: Using the job aid, what do you check before you run a payment a second time?
options: That the tenant is on AutoPay
questions.explanation: Never run a pending payment twice: it can charge the tenant twice.

questions.q: A tenant surprised by a small first bill should be told everyone pays on the 1st and the first month was shortened.
questions.explanation: True. First-of-month billing shortens the first month to match; it is not a discount.
